summary.text: Chuck Hubbard is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Virginia Foxx in North Carolina's 5th Congressional District.
A Wilkes County native, he spent more than forty years as a local journalist at the Wilkes Journal-Patriot, the newspaper his grandfather founded, according to his campaign website.
He says he is running on affordability, public education, and protecting Medicare, Medicaid and Social Security.

paragraphs.text: Hubbard was born in Bryson City, North Carolina, and describes himself as a native of Wilkes County with family roots across the state.
He graduated from Wilkes Central High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Wofford College in 1985.

According to his campaign website, he began working at age 8 in the print shop of the Wilkes Journal-Patriot, a newspaper founded by his grandfather, began covering news for it at 16 as a student, and joined full-time after college.
The Yadkin Ripple reported that his grandfather founded the paper in 1932.
Hubbard worked as a journalist for more than forty years, according to his campaign website.
In 2025 he said he planned to run for North Carolina's 5th District in 2026, and he won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary, defeating Kyah Creekmore, 56.7% to 43.3%.
He has served on the boards of the Wilkes Recovery Revolution, the Wilkes Child Abuse Prevention Team and the Wilkes Prison Ministry.
His campaign site says he lives with his wife Shari, who served over twenty years as a State Trooper, and that they have three daughters and two grandchildren.

sources.title: Wilkes County native launches campaign for Congress
